victim.name: Ronald Paul "Ronnie" Jack
victim.occupation: millworker (recently unemployed due to back injury)
victim.note: Disappeared with his family on the night of August 1-2, 1980, from Prince George, British Columbia. No trace of any of them was ever located. Represents the primary case figure — see 'missing_family' for the other three. Also missing with him: Doreen Jack (26, partner/mother), Russell Jack (9, child), and Ryan Jack (4, child) — all four disappeared together and none was ever located.

suspects.name: Unknown Man from the Bar
suspects.note: Tall, heavyset Caucasian man in his late 30s with reddish-brown hair and a full beard; wore a baseball cap, red checkered work shirt, and a blue waist-length nylon jacket with an orange logo later associated with a forestry-equipment brand. Never identified.

suspects.name: Unrelated Third Party (Hypothetical)
suspects.note: Represents the hypothesis that the unknown man's presence was coincidental and a separate person or group was actually responsible.

timeline.event: Ronnie visits a local pub in Prince George
An unidentified man enters the pub and speaks with Ronnie
Ronnie and the unknown man leave the pub in the man's dark 4x4 pickup truck
They travel roughly 350 metres to the Jack family home
Phone records show Ronnie calling his brother and discussing the job
Doreen's cousin visits and sees her packing supplies for several weeks; the unknown man is inside the property
Doreen's cousin leaves after about an hour at the home
Phone records confirm a call made from the Jack family residence
Ronnie, Doreen, Russell, and Ryan disappear

evidence.name: Pub Witness Account
evidence.description: True eyewitness account establishing the meeting between Ronnie and the unknown man.

evidence.name: Unknown Man's Physical Description
evidence.description: True but incomplete; provides the main identification pattern for the unknown man.

evidence.name: Dark 4x4 Pickup Observation
evidence.description: True eyewitness account linking the man and Ronnie to the journey home.

evidence.name: 11:16 PM Phone Call
evidence.description: Shows Ronnie contacted his brother and discussed the job offer.

evidence.name: Doreen's Cousin's Visit
evidence.description: Places the unknown man inside the home while Doreen packed.

evidence.name: 1:21 AM Residence Call
evidence.description: Establishes another communication from the family residence shortly before the disappearance.

evidence.name: School Registration Records
evidence.description: Russell was registered to start school weeks after the disappearance — evidence against the idea the family had simply abandoned their planned lives.

evidence.name: Family Belongings
evidence.description: The family took clothing sufficient for roughly two weeks — supports short-term preparation but does not establish what happened after departure.

evidence.name: Police Report / Initial Theory
evidence.description: Documents the early assumption that Ronnie may have found work and left voluntarily.

evidence.name: Incorrect 'Family Found' Report
evidence.description: Shows a major investigative communication failure — the family had not actually been found.

evidence.name: Logging-Camp Interviews/Searches
evidence.description: Later efforts to locate the alleged workplace; no camp matching the description was confirmed.

evidence.name: Husqvarna Jacket-Logo Lead
evidence.description: Unverified — the jacket logo was reportedly identified as a forestry-equipment supply brand, suggesting a possible genuine forestry connection but not establishing identity or a genuine job offer.

evidence.name: Reward / Public Appeals
evidence.description: Shows later attempts to generate new information from the public.

evidence.name: Later Searches and Excavations
evidence.description: No trace of the family was ever located according to the source material.

puzzles.name: Night Timeline & Witness Description
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the sequence from the bar encounter through the family's disappearance, and assemble the unknown man's physical description and clothing from witness information.

puzzles.name: Job Offer Audit & Packing Analysis
puzzles.description: Separate what was actually observed about the job offer from assumptions about whether it was genuine, and determine what the family's preparation suggests and what it cannot establish.

puzzles.name: Logging Camp Search
puzzles.description: Compare the alleged location and job details with information from forestry workers and searches.

puzzles.name: Investigation Failure
puzzles.description: Investigate the incorrect report that the family had been found and identify how that affected the case.

puzzles.name: Alternative Hypotheses & Final Uncertainty Report
puzzles.description: Compare accident, voluntary disappearance, abduction/foul play, and unrelated-unknown-man hypotheses, then state what can be established, what is plausible, and what remains unknown.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Should not manufacture a culprit when the underlying case is unresolved. Adaptation changes hints, evidence order, framing, and difficulty — not the facts.
puzzles.design_constraint: 'Insufficient evidence to determine what happened' is a valid, rewarded final conclusion. The evaluator rewards epistemic discipline: knowing what the evidence proves, what it suggests, and what it cannot establish.

hypotheses.statement: The family voluntarily left for genuine employment and later became unreachable.
The job offer was fabricated and the family was deliberately lured away from home.
The family travelled to a remote location and suffered an accident or other event.
The unknown man was directly involved in the family's disappearance.
The unknown man's presence was coincidental and is not connected to the disappearance.
Another person or group was responsible, while the unknown man is only one part of the story.
